The active power, in watts, delivered to the load is _______ (round off to nearest integer).

raw_record.original_question: Consider an ideal full-bridge single-phase DC-AC inverter with a DC bus voltage magnitude of 1000 V. The inverter output voltage \(v(t)\), shown in the image, is obtained when diagonal switches of the inverter are switched with 50% duty cycle. The inverter feeds a load with a sinusoidal current given by \(i(t) = 10\sin(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{3})\,A\), where \(\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}\). The active power, in watts, delivered to the load is _______ (round off to nearest integer).
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, v(t) is a periodic square wave, and the horizontal axis marks 0, 0.5T, T; within one period, the voltage is at a positive level from 0 to 0.5T, and at a negative level from 0.5T to T, then repeats with period T.

Reasoning: The ideal full-bridge bipolar output voltage amplitude is taken as Vdc=1000 V. The fundamental wave of this 50% duty-cycle square wave is v1(t)=(4Vdc/π)sin(ωt). The load current i(t)=10sin(ωt−π/3) A contains only the fundamental frequency, so the average active power is produced only by the interaction between the voltage fundamental and the current, and the average power of higher harmonics is zero. The RMS value of the voltage fundamental is V1,rms=(4×1000/π)/√2, the RMS current is Irms=10/√2, and the phase difference between the voltage fundamental and the current is π/3. Therefore P=V1,rms Irms cos(π/3); substituting and rounding according to the problem requirement gives P≈3181 W.
